facts.content: Patient reports left-sided hearing loss with ringing in the ear.
facts.source_text: “I can’t really hear as well as I used to”—left-sided hearing loss with ringing in the ear.

facts.content: Symptoms have been present for approximately six weeks.
Hearing loss and tinnitus affect only the left ear; the right ear is normal.
facts.source_text: • Laterality: Left ear only; right ear normal.

facts.content: The decreased hearing and tinnitus are intermittent.
facts.source_text: • Quality: Intermittent decreased hearing and tinnitus (“ringing”).

facts.content: Watching TV or listening to music can trigger the ringing.
facts.source_text: • Triggers: Watching TV or listening to music can “set off” the ringing.

facts.content: Patient experiences occasional mild dizziness or feeling off-balance.
facts.source_text: • Associated symptoms: Occasional mild dizziness/feeling off-balance;

facts.content: Patient denies true vertigo.
Patient denies nausea.
Patient denies chest pain.
Patient denies palpitations.
Patient denies ear pain.
Patient denies ear discharge.
Patient denies ear pruritus.
Patient denies documented fever.
There was a brief, self-limited hearing issue lasting about two days approximately one year ago.
facts.source_text: • Prior episode: Brief (~2 days) self-limited hearing issue ~1 year ago.

facts.content: Patient does not use cotton-bud ear cleaning.
facts.source_text: • No use of cotton-bud ear cleaning.

facts.content: Positive decreased hearing in the left ear.
Positive tinnitus in the left ear.
Positive mild dizziness.
Negative fevers.
Negative chest pain.
Negative palpitations.
Negative otalgia.
Negative otorrhea.
Negative ear pruritus.
No medications are reported.
No in-person physical examination was performed during this telemedicine visit.
facts.source_text: Physical Examination: No in-person exam performed (telemedicine visit).

facts.content: Vitals were not documented.
No diagnostics were obtained during the visit.
Assessment: left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent mild dizziness.
facts.source_text: 1. Left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent mild dizziness.

facts.content: Differential includes impacted cerumen, otitis media/externa, early sensorineural hearing loss, and inner-ear (vestibular) disorder; etiology uncertain pending otoscopic examination.
facts.source_text: • Consider impacted cerumen vs otitis media/externa vs early sensorineural hearing loss vs inner-ear (vestibular) disorder. Etiology uncertain pending otoscopic examination.

facts.content: Arrange face-to-face clinic visit within four to five days for otoscopic examination and cerumen evaluation.
facts.source_text: • Arrange face-to-face clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic exam and cerumen evaluation.

facts.content: Provide patient with an educational leaflet link on tinnitus and encourage review before the visit.
facts.source_text: • Provide patient with educational leaflet link on tinnitus; encourage review prior to visit.

facts.content: If cerumen impaction is confirmed, perform ear-syringing or micro-suction according to clinic protocol.
facts.source_text: • If cerumen impaction confirmed: perform ear-syringing or micro-suction per clinic protocol.

facts.content: If there is no obstruction, proceed with further work-up including audiometry with or without ENT referral.
facts.source_text: • If no obstruction: proceed with further work-up (audiometry ± ENT referral).

facts.content: Advise patient to re-book a video consult if symptoms worsen or new symptoms occur.
facts.source_text: • Safety-netting: Advise patient to re-book video consult if symptoms worsen or new symptoms (vertigo, severe pain, discharge, persistent dizziness) occur.

facts.content: Patient to call the support team to schedule the appointment.
facts.source_text: • Patient to call support team (number left in note) to schedule appointment.

facts.content: Disposition is outpatient.
Patient will have follow-up after the examination.
